 Judgment
The petition is filed seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- for the injuries sustained during road traffic accident.

2. Petition averments in brief are as follows; That on 17.12.2019 at about 06.00 PM., while the petitioner was riding his motor cycle along with his wife, near Deepa Bar Bidarahalli, the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA- 53-B-9950 came from opposite direction, dashed to petitioner's motor Manjunath vs Baba Transport on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82121087/
1 cycle causing injuries to the right side of the petitioner.
He was admitted as an inpatient and has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospital, medicine and etc.,
Due to the injuries he cannot walk, squat or sit on the floor and unable to do any manual work.
That he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- by working as coolie and lost the same.
Hence prays to grant compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.

3. The respondent No.2 appeared and denied the averments of the petition and also submits that the petitioner had no driving license to drive the vehicle nor there was insurance and that there is negligence on the part of the petitioner for the accident and accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of the Pleadings and materials, the following issues were framed.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 17.12.2019 at about 06.00 PM, when the petitioner was riding on motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-EB-6620, near Deepa bar, bidarahalli, Bangalore East taluk, Bangalore, while a Lorry bearing No.KA-53-B-9950, came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner motor cycle, as a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In order to substantiate the allegation, the petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and one witness examined as PW-2 and has produced 15 documents on his behalf.
The respondent got examined one witness as RW-1 and has produced 2 documents on his behalf.

6. Heard from the counsel for the petitioner and the respondent.
7.

My findings on the above points are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  8. Point No.1:

According to the petitioner, on 17.12.2019 at about 06.00 PM., while the petitioner was Manjunath vs Baba Transport on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82121087/
2 riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-EB-6620 along with his wife, near Deepa Bar Bidarahalli,
the driver of the lorry bearing NO.KA-53-B-9950 came from opposite direction dashed to petitioner's motor cycle causing injuries to the right side of the petitioner.

He was admitted to East point Hospital where in first aid treatment was taken and later admitted to Sri.Sathya Sai Orthopaedic Multi Speciality Hospital and then referred to Shanti Clinic, Mysore road, Bangalore for further treatment.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopaedic Multi Speciality Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: That petitioner was admitted as an inpatient and has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospital, medicine and etc., That due to the injuries he cannot walk, squat or sit on the floor and unable to do any manual work.
That he has suffered multiple fractures and was in bed rest for a period of 6 months.
That he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- by working as coolie.
That a case in Cr.No.349/2019 has been lodged by the Avalahalli police station against the driver of the aforesaid vehicle.

Hence prays to grant compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.
9.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and filed affidavit in lieu of examination in chief.
He has produced 10 documents on his behalf, out of which, the FIS is produced as Ex.P.2.

As per Ex.P.2, the wife of the petitioner has lodged complaint on the next day of the accident in the police station at about 11.00 AM., alleging that while she was pillion rider along with her husband, riding the motor cycle, the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner caused accident, by which her husband was injured to the right side ear and to the face.
That he was immediately taken to hospital for treatment and thus has sought for compensation.
Further the copy of FIR in Cr.No. 349/2019, alleging offences punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC is produced as Ex.P.1.
The spot panchanama is produced as Ex.P.3 where the lorry and two wheeler were found on the spot on the next day of the accident.

The MVA report is shown to have damaged towards front right side bumper scratched to the offending vehicle and head light and rear left side saree guard rod has been damaged, to the petitioner's vehicle.
The report is given that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the above said vehicle.
The Wound Certificate from Sri.Satya Sai orthopeadic hospital shows the alleged history of RTA of two wheeler versus truck on 17.12.2019.

The final report is as per Ex.P.6, alleging offences punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC in Cr.No.349/2019.
10.
The main allegation of the respondent is that there is negligence on the part of the petitioner in causing the accident, since he had no driving license and insurance to the said vehicle.
Therefore in this regard apart from cross examination of the petitioner / PW-1, the respondent NO.2 also got examined the manager of the respondent No.2 as RW-1.

This RW-1 has deposed that while driver of respondent No.1 was riding the vehicle slowly, the petitioner suddenly drove his vehicle and dashed to the vehicle of the respondent No.2 causing the accident.
That there is a delay of one day, where the petitioner has completely utilized to concoct and create case with false intention and illegal manner.
That he is not having driving license and there was no insurance to his vehicle and thus prays to dismiss the petition.
11. With these defence the PW-1 was cross examined by the counsel for the respondent.
He submits that the said road width was of about allowing 2 heavy motor vehicles to travel in the said road and that there is hump near the place of the accident.
He further has denied all other allegation made against him regarding negligence and clearly submits that there was no injuries to the vehicle driven by him.

He also admits that he had neither driving license to drive the said vehicle nor there is RC Manjunath vs Baba Transport on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82121087/
3 book to the said vehicle.
12.

In this context the counsel for the respondent though did not appear for arguments at final stage submitted during course of cross examination that there is negligence on the part of the petitioner,
who has driven the vehicle in the busy road without following traffic rules of the MV Act and thus has sought for dismissal of the petition.
The RW-1 is not an eye witness to the accident, but has collected the documents from concerned police station.
Therefore the evidence lead by the RW-1 when compared to the evidence of petitioner goes in effective.
The Wound Certificate marked as Ex.P.6 is very much clear to the fact that the petitioner was admitted with the history of RTA between 2 wheeler and the truck.
The alleged truck was found on the spot and there is head on collusion in between two vehicles.
Therefore there is complete negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., the lorry.

13. In the very recent decision of the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.101921/2019, dt.
15.09.2021, in divisional manager, Cholamandalam insurance company Pvt. Ltd., Vs. Nagava an another, the Hon'ble High court has clearly held that if the person having no driving license to drive the vehicle, trial court have to consider 35% contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner's themselves in causing the accident.

entities.text: divisional manager, Cholamandalam insurance company Pvt. Ltd., Vs. Nagava an another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence in view of above said authority, when the petitioner himself has clearly admitted that he had no driving license to drive the vehicles and has also admitted that he was driving along with his wife as pillion rider, there is contributory negligence on his part which is to an extent of 35%.
Therefore the above issue is answered in partly affirmative.
14. Point No.2:

The copy of Adhaar card pertaining to the petitioner is produced as Ex.P.7, showing his year of birth as 1980 and thus his age as on the date of the accident was 39 years and appropriate multiplier for the said age is 15.
what is the future loss of income for the petitioner is to be seen.
Regarding monthly income, the petitioner not produced any document and hence notional income of Rs.13,250/- can be considered as monthly income.
15. The petitioner submits that due to the accident he is unable to do manual work and was in bed rest for about 6 months.

That he has underwent treatment at local hospitals near his place after getting discharged from Sri.Sathya Sai Orthopedic multi specialty Hospital and has also undergone treatment at Ayurvedic hospital.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopedic multi specialty Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: No documents are produced by the petitioner to show his further treatment taken either in ayurvedic hospital or in any other hospital.

The petitioner got produced the Wound Certificate pertaining to Sri.Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital, marked as Ex.P.5, where it is shown that the petitioner sustained injury to facial region and right shoulders.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The medical bills pertaining to the said hospital are produced as Ex.P.9 wherein the petitioner is shown to have undergone CT Brain and face with 3D reconstruction etc.,
In this regard, petitioner also tried to summon the hospital authority of Sri.Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital and got examined as PW-2.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The PW-2 got produced the documents which are discharge summary,
inpatient records etc., as Ex.P.13 and P.14, X-ray as Ex.P.15.

A perusal of Ex.P.13 to P.15 goes to show that one Mr.Manjunath was admitted in their hospital from 24.01.2020 and discharged on 26.01.2020, where it is also shown that the said Manjunath aged about 32 yeas was admitted with Manjunath vs Baba Transport on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82121087/
4 the history of RTA of 2 wheeler Vs 6 wheeler, near budigere village main road and has sustained injury to left leg region.
These documents are completely against the documents produced by the petitioner where the petitioner met with an accident on 17.12.2019.
A person cannot be expected to have surgery after period of nearly one month from the date of accident.
Signature of the petitioner on the petition and with consent letter given to left leg surgery are completely different.

There is no history of fracture of left leg or fracture of any leg with regard to the petitioner in Wound Certificate,
who was admitted to the hospital i.e.,Sri.Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital on 07.12.2019 and was discharged on the very next day of admission from the said hospital.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: By all these admissions it is very much clear that the PW-2 has produced the documents pertaining to some other persons by name Manjunath and does not belong to the petitioner.
16. On going through the Wound Certificate, I note that the petitioner got discharged himself as against the medical advise.
As per the said Wound Certificate, the petitioner has suffered injuries to face and right shoulder.
Except this no material is placed by the petitioner to show the details of the injuries, he sustained from the said accident.
Though the counsel for the petitioner tried to summon several doctors, the doctor did not appear nor petitioners themselves failed to pay proper fee.
Therefore there is no assessment of disability of the petitioner.
Even there is no fracture to the leg or the hand or to any other bones causing the disability.
The counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is suffering from neuro problems.
Even filed application to summon the neuro surgeon.
But did not pay the fees to summon the doctor and thus judgment was postponed.

But finally when there was no proceeding from the counsel for the petitioner to bring the said neurologist or the neuro surgeon to give evidence, prayer of the counsel for the petitioner was rejected and posted for judgment.
17. In this situation, when there is only facial disability, the fact that the petitioner was under the bed rest for a period of 6 months cannot be believed.
Why he was on the said rest and for which injuries he was under bed rest for a period of 6 months is not explained by the petitioner.

It is important to note that after getting discharged from Sri.Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital, the petitioner though has submitted that he underwent treatment in different hospitals has not produced any document.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopeadic multi specialty Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: However considering the fact that the petitioner met with the trauma of accident and the facial injuries suffered, this court can consider the laid up period of the petitioner for a period of one month.
Therefore in this situation the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income.

18. As per the available materials on record, Ex.P9, the medical expenses would tune to Rs.15,160/-,
which he is entitled under the head of medical expenses and hospital charges.
19.
As per the Wound Certificate produced as Ex.P5, the petitioner had sustained injury to facial region and right shoulder which are grievous in nature.
The petitioner was hospitalized only for one day on 17.12.2019.
Thus he was in the hospital as inpatient for one day and may be expected to be in the complete bed rest for one month.

Thus the petitioner can be made entitled for Rs.25,000/-
towards pain and sufferings, Rs.500/- towards food and nourishment charges, Rs.1,000/- towards conveyance charges, and Rs.1,000/- towards attendant charges and Rs.13,250/- towards loss of amenities.
Manjunath vs Baba Transport on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82121087/
5 20.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable compensation as under:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs.25,000/- 2 Medical expenses and hospital charges Rs.15,160/- 3 Food and nourishment Rs.500/- 4 Conveyance charges Rs.1,000/- 5 Attendant charges Rs.1,000/- 6 Loss of amenities Rs.13,250/- 7 Loss of income during laid up period Rs.13,250/-
TOTAL Rs.69,160/-
In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.69,160/-.

That after deduction of 35% contributory negligence, the petitioner is entitled for net compensation of Rs.44,954/- which can be rounded to Rs.45,000/-.
21.
In this case, there is no disputed fact that the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said lorry bearing No.KA-53-B-9950 which caused accident.
The respondent no.2 has failed to prove that the insurance company is not liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount and as on the date of accident the insurance policy was in force.
Hence, this issue is answered accordingly burdening the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner, along with the present Bank rate of interest at 6%.
22. Point No.3:

For the reasons stated in the aforesaid paragraphs, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.45,000/- with interest at 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization of the entire amount.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within two months from the date of judgment.
After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.5,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
